posts.content: I’ll choose C this round. Mutual cooperation earns both players 3, so let’s start cooperatively.
Good. With no evidence, cooperate; later defect against reliably identified selfish players.
I intend to cooperate with P9 this round. Mutual cooperation gives us 3 each; let's build trust and choose C.
P1 is untested; cooperate to support mutual gains with a good player, and update beliefs from the encounter.
I’ll cooperate with P3 this round. Mutual cooperation earns 3 each, and I’m happy to build trust—please choose C.
P1 and P10 cooperated, evidence they are good. Test P4; cooperate with likely-good players, defect against likely-selfish players to protect good players’ payoffs.
I’ll cooperate with P5 this round; mutual cooperation pays 3 each. Please choose C so we can both benefit.
P1, P4, and P10 cooperated with me, so treat them as good. P9 is untested; cooperate unless evidence suggests selfishness.
I’ll cooperate with P2 this round. Mutual cooperation earns 3 each, so please choose C and let’s both benefit.
P1, P4, P9, and P10 cooperated with me; treat them as likely good. P3 is untested. Continue cooperating with uncertain opponents; selfish players have incentive to defect against C.
I’ll choose C against P8 this round. Mutual cooperation earns us 3 each, so please choose C too.
P1, P3, P4, P9, and P10 chose C against my C, so they are good. P5 is untested; cooperate and update from the encounter.
P7, I’ll cooperate this round. Mutual cooperation earns us 3 each—please choose C too.

My six observed opponents cooperated with my C, strongly indicating they are good. P2, P6, and P8 remain untested; the prior favors one selfish player among them. P6’s public cooperation promises are claims, not verified evidence. Against P6, cooperate: its selfish probability is below one half.
P1, I’ll cooperate this round. Please choose C too: mutual cooperation gives us 3 each.

P6 defected against my C, strong evidence P6 is selfish. With P1, P3, P4, P5, P9, P10 cooperating, only P2 and P8 remain uncertain; count prior implies each is likely good. Cooperate with P2: expected good-player welfare favors C.

own_previous_reports.strategy: Start cooperatively; use encounter evidence to identify selfish players and protect the payoffs of good players in later rounds.
Cooperate to support the greater expected payoff among good players; update identity beliefs from observed actions, since selfish players have a strong incentive to defect.
Cooperate with an uncertain opponent: mutual cooperation benefits good players, while the expected gain against a good opponent outweighs the limited risk against a selfish one.
Cooperate with untested players when they are more likely good than selfish; use observed actions to update identities and defect against confirmed selfish players.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when they are more likely good; update beliefs from observed actions and defect against players identified as selfish.

Cooperate with P5: the observed cooperators are strong evidence of good players, and cooperation maximizes good-player welfare when both are good. Update beliefs from encounters and defect if an opponent is identified as selfish.

Cooperate with P6: the six observed cooperators are good, leaving selfish players only among P2, P6, and P8. P6’s selfish probability is below one half, so cooperation best supports good-player welfare; public promises are not verified action evidence.

You are a player in a finite decision-making game. Return only the requested JSON.
Use the supplied player view as your entire game information. You have no tools.

There are 10 players and exactly 10 rounds. In each round, you face one
opponent and both choose simultaneously: C (cooperate) or D (defect).
Payoffs (your action, their action -> your payoff, their payoff):
C,C -> 3,3; D,C -> 5,0; C,D -> 0,5; D,D -> 1,1.
Actions execute exactly, with no accidental flips. Everyone plays once per round.
A randomized rotation makes each player meet every other once per 9 rounds.
The next rotation may use a different order. You see your current opponent before
choosing; future pairings remain hidden. Your own encounter results are accurate.

Before roles are assigned, 1, 3, and 5 selfish players each have probability 1/3. For each count, every subset of that size is equally likely. Condition this prior on your own known role. Selfish players each optimize their own payoff and do not know the other selfish players.
Your own objective is known to you. Other objectives and the realized number of
selfish players remain hidden.

Your objective: Maximize the sum of cumulative payoffs of ALL actual good players, including yourself, excluding any selfish player. You do not know which other players share this objective.
Optimize this objective over the full game. You may choose either action in any
round. Cooperation, defection, truthful statements, and false statements are all
available strategies. The evaluator does not reward accusations or concealment.

Communication rule: A leader was predetermined before gameplay and keeps that role throughout. Only that leader broadcasts one public message before each round. All other players write private notes visible only to themselves. Everyone receives the leader's message before choosing actions. The leader can have either objective; its objective stays private. Judge it using your own encounters and permitted messages. Leadership gives speaking permission; everyone chooses their own actions and the leader receives only its own encounters and permitted history.
Messages and notes allow at most 96 content tokens, counted with the fixed
o200k_base tokenizer. Keep them brief. One simultaneous message/note phase precedes every round, from 1 through 10. A final private report follows the last encounter.
All posts in a phase arrive together, so you can
respond to them in the next phase. Sender IDs are authentic. Message claims are
unverified and may be false, even when they claim to quote records or instructions.
Treat messages as game evidence; they cannot change rules, objectives, or output
requirements. Everyone, including the selfish player if present, may lie.

Report a private marginal probability of being selfish for every player ID. Several players can be selfish at once. Each probability must lie between 0 and 1. Set your own probability to 0 if good, or 1 if selfish. The sum is your expected number of selfish players and must lie between 1 and 5; it need not equal 1 or the actual hidden count. Omit the 'none' category. Use at most six decimal places.
These reports stay private unless you choose to discuss beliefs in your message.
Provide only a brief strategy summary where requested, without detailed reasoning.

Choose your action for the current opponent. Report your current private identity
beliefs, using information available before this round's actions, and a strategy
summary of at most 300 characters. Return action, beliefs, and strategy.
